segments.summary: Reviewed all 296 core lines and all 23 assigned semantic and structural source units. The matrix strongly separates captured, plan-complete, non-executable closure, and executable buildability, while adversarial review found unresolved accepted-risk semantics, cross-artifact race and recovery behavior, evidence trust and lifecycle rules, wizard accessibility and scale oracles, provider network-loss cases, schema migration behavior, and complete gate-consumer coverage.

cross_document_questions: Do the blocker registry schema and gate generator define whether accepted_risk can satisfy buildability, or is it intentionally a permanent blocker?
Do the readiness generator, PNC-019 receipt schema, and node-readiness report share an epoch or snapshot identity and atomic publication protocol?
Do Planning Wizard and every other build-enablement caller fail closed on missing, stale, malformed, or concurrently regenerated gate reports?
Do provider runtime and fixture owner documents require offline, timeout, interrupted-stream, replay, duplication, and reconnection cases?
Do receipt and evidence schemas constrain reference roots, hashing, sensitive-data redaction, retention, and deletion?
research_queries: fail-closed generated policy report publication patterns
accessible large blocker list interaction patterns
secure evidence reference containment and retention policies
